key_insight: The paper extends human-in-the-loop Bayesian optimization by turning constraint satisfaction and robustness into explicit Pareto objectives, letting experts choose among trade-offs instead of accepting a single automatic recommendation.
engineering_relevance: This enables safer and more practical bioprocess development by identifying operating conditions that are not only high-performing but also feasible and resilient to input variability.
method: Extend Pareto Front Guided Sampling (PFGS) with GP-based multi-objective reformulation.
Add an analytic objective for posterior probability of meeting output specification limits.
Add a Monte Carlo robustness objective based on expected lower-confidence performance under input perturbations.
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated on an eight-dimensional fed-batch CHO cell culture simulator, where it finds high-performing, constraint-compliant, and perturbation-resilient operating conditions.
watch_item: The approach depends on Gaussian process surrogate quality and Monte Carlo estimates, so performance may be sensitive to surrogate misspecification and computational cost as dimensionality or uncertainty grows.
paper_title: A Human-in-the-Loop Bayesian Optimization Framework for Constraint-Aware Bioprocess Development
